titulo: Adjectives and possessives: Adjectives: the table

aula.objetivo: Make the adjective and the possessive agree with the noun in gender and number, using the table of endings.

blocos.texto: (or: the scissors method — how to memorise ONE adjective and know FOUR)

blocos.titulo: The adjective: the concept and the fixed-root rule
blocos.explicacao: What is an adjective? The grab test. Before any table, a simple question: what is an adjective? An adjective is the word that completes the noun. It is the quality, the characteristic, the way the thing is. And there is an infallible test for recognising it: the grab test. Can you pick up «big» in your hand? No. Can you pick up «new» in your hand? No. Can you pick up «yellow» in your hand? No. But you can pick up a big thing, a new house, a yellow car. You pick up the thing, never the quality. A quality that exists only attached to a noun = adjective. This holds for new, old, tall, short, yellow, red, beautiful, ugly, expensive, cheap, hot, cold, intelligent, strange. They are all adjectives. They all need a noun to exist. And that is why the adjective agrees with the noun. If the noun is masculine, the adjective is masculine. If the noun is feminine, the adjective is feminine. If it is neuter, the adjective is neuter. English adjectives never change, so for you this is new: in Russian, the agreement is very visible, because the ending of the adjective changes clearly and systematically. The golden rule: the root never changes. Here is the information that will set you free. Remember this: every Russian adjective is a LEGO of two pieces: ROOT (untouchable) + ENDING (movable). The root carries the meaning. The ending carries the grammar. So when the adjective has to change gender (masculine → feminine → neuter), the root stays still and only the ending moves. Here is how it looks in Russian with the adjective «new»: The root НОВ- never changed. Only the ending. Always.

tabelas.titulo: The golden rule: the root never changes

blocos.titulo: The "scissors" method: how never to get it wrong again
blocos.explicacao: The "scissors" method: how never to get it wrong again. Now the method that will be your tool for the rest of your life. I call it the "scissors": Cut the last two letters of the masculine. You have the root. Paste the new ending. Done — the adjective has changed gender. It works because the masculine endings — -ЫЙ, -ОЙ, -ИЙ — have exactly two letters each. It is a perfect fit. See it in practice: Adjective: но́вый (new) • 1. Cut the last two letters: но́в (root) • 2. Paste the feminine ending: но́в + ая = но́вая • 3. Paste the neuter ending: но́в + ое = но́вое • 4. Paste the plural ending: но́в + ые = но́вые Adjective: большо́й (big) • 1. Cut the last two letters: больш (root) • 2. Paste the feminine ending: больш + а́я = больша́я • 3. Paste the neuter ending: больш + о́е = большо́е • 4. Paste the plural ending: больш + и́е = больши́е Adjective: си́ний (blue) • 1. Cut the last two letters: син (root) • 2. Paste the feminine ending: син + яя = си́няя • 3. Paste the neuter ending: син + ее = си́нее • 4. Paste the plural ending: син + ие = си́ние Did you notice? It is always the same operation. Cut two letters, paste the new one. Always. It never fails. The conclusion that is worth the whole lesson: if you know ONE adjective — the masculine — you know all FOUR. Always memorise the masculine. It is a 75% discount. Want to test it? Take ста́рый (old). Cut the last two letters: ста́р. Now build: ста́р + ая = ста́рая ста́р + ое = ста́рое ста́р + ые = ста́рые You have just learned four forms of an adjective in three seconds. The goal is this: you build the form, instead of merely memorising the ready-made table.

The three masculine endings. Before applying the scissors, you need to know which masculine ending the adjective has. There are three possibilities, and each one tells you which "family" the adjective belongs to. • 1. -ЫЙ (the most common) The vast majority of adjectives. Always -ЫЙ in the masculine. но́вый (new) ста́рый (old) краси́вый (beautiful) у́мный (intelligent) холо́дный (cold) дешёвый (cheap) ве́рный (faithful) дли́нный (long) • 2. -ОЙ (when the stress falls on the ending) You recognise it because the stress is at the end. Always -ОЙ in the masculine. большо́й (big) молодо́й (young) дорого́й (expensive) плохо́й (bad) просто́й (simple) родно́й (dear, native) Note: even though it is -ОЙ, you cut the last two letters. The root is БОЛЬШ-, МОЛОД-, ДОРОГ-, ПЛОХ-, ПРОСТ-, РОДН-. • 3. -ИЙ (adjectives with a "special" root) There are two reasons for an adjective to end in -ИЙ: a) Adjectives whose root ends in г, к, х (the throaty consonants). After these consonants, Ы is never written — И is written. It is a Russian spelling rule: ру́сский (Russian) — root РУССК- ма́ленький (small) — root МАЛЕНЬК- ди́кий (wild) — root ДИК- стро́гий (strict) — root СТРОГ- ти́хий (quiet) — root ТИХ- These adjectives behave like ordinary adjectives in the feminine and the neuter: ру́сский → ру́сская → ру́сское ма́ленький → ма́ленькая → ма́ленькое b) The truly "soft" adjectives — the family of синий. A small but important group: си́ний (blue) после́дний (last) у́тренний (morning) вече́рний (evening) весе́нний (spring) зи́мний (winter) ле́тний (summer) осе́нний (autumn) These behave differently: си́ний → си́няя → си́нее (not "си́ная" nor "си́ное"!) после́дний → после́дняя → после́днее It is the only real exception at the start of your studies.

blocos.titulo: The adjective changes with the noun
blocos.explicacao: The adjective comes before the noun and copies its gender and number. To find the form, start from the masculine (-ый, -ий or -ой) and change the ending: feminine -ая (or -яя), neuter -ое (or -ее), plural -ые (or -ие). After г, к, х, ж, ч, ш, щ you get -ий / -ие (маленький, маленькие, хороший, хорошие). The plural is the same for all three genders. There are four types of adjective, which only change the way the same idea is written: hard (-ый), stressed at the end (-ой), after г/к/х/ж/ч/ш/щ (-ий, and the neuter -ое with stress or -ее without stress) and soft (-ий, -яя, -ее).
blocos.comparacao: English adjectives never change («new house», «new houses»), but in Russian there is one form for each of the three genders and another for the plural.
